investorCharter.title: Investor Charter for Investment Advisers
investorCharter.subtitle: The rights, responsibilities, and service standards SEBI requires every registered Investment Adviser to disclose to clients.

sections.heading: A. Vision and Mission Statements for Investors
list: Vision — Invest with knowledge & safety.
Mission — Every investor should be able to invest in right investment products based on their needs, manage and monitor them to meet their goals, access reports and enjoy financial wellness.

sections.heading: B. Details of Business Transacted by the Investment Adviser with Respect to the Investors
list: To enter into an agreement with the client providing all details including fee details, aspects of Conflict of interest disclosure and maintaining confidentiality of information.
To do a proper and unbiased risk-profiling and suitability assessment of the client.
To conduct audit annually.
To disclose the status of complaints on its website.

To disclose the name, proprietor name, type of registration, registration number, validity, complete address with telephone numbers and associated SEBI Office details (i.e. Head office/ regional/ local Office) on its website.
To employ only qualified and certified employees.
To deal with clients only from official number.
To maintain records of interactions, with all clients including prospective clients (prior to onboarding), where any conversation related to advice has taken place.
To ensure that all advertisements are in adherence to the provisions of the Advertisement Code for Investment Advisers.
Not to discriminate in terms of services provided, among clients opting for same/similar products/services offered by investment adviser.

sections.heading: C. Details of Services Provided to Investors (No Indicative Timelines) — Onboarding of Clients
list: Sharing of agreement copy.
Completing KYC of clients.

sections.heading: C. Details of Services Provided to Investors — Disclosure to Clients
list: To provide full disclosure about its business, affiliations, compensation in the agreement.
To not access client's accounts or holdings for offering advice.
To disclose the risk profile to the client.
To disclose any conflict of interest of the investment advisory activities with any other activities of the investment adviser.
To disclose the extent of use of Artificial Intelligence tools in providing investment advisory services.

sections.heading: C. Details of Services Provided to Investors — Other Obligations
list: To provide investment advice to the client based on the risk-profiling of the clients and suitability of the client.
To treat all advisory clients with honesty and integrity.
To make adequate disclosure to the investor of all material facts such as risks, obligations, costs, etc. relating to the products or securities advised by the adviser.
To provide clear guidance and adequate caution notice to clients when providing investment advice for dealing in complex and high-risk financial products/services.

To ensure confidentiality of information shared by clients unless such information is required to be provided in furtherance of discharging legal obligations or a client has provided specific consent to share such information.
To disclose the timelines for the various services provided by the investment adviser to clients and ensure adherence to the said timelines.

sections.heading: D. Details of Grievance Redressal Mechanism and How to Access It
paragraphs: An investor can lodge a complaint/grievance against an Investment Adviser in the following ways:
list: Mode of filing the complaint with investment adviser — In case of any grievance/complaint, an investor may approach the concerned Investment Adviser who shall strive to redress the grievance immediately, but not later than 21 days of the receipt of the grievance.

Mode of filing the complaint on SCORES or with Investment Adviser Administration and Supervisory Body (IAASB) — SCORES 2.0 (a web based centralized grievance redressal system of SEBI for facilitating effective grievance redressal in time-bound manner). Two level review for complaint/grievance against investment adviser: first review done by designated body (IAASB), second review done by SEBI. A complaint may also be lodged by email to the designated email ID of IAASB.

If the Investor is not satisfied with the resolution provided by the Market Participants, then the Investor has the option to file the complaint/grievance on SMARTODR platform for its resolution through online conciliation or arbitration.

With regard to physical complaints, investors may send their complaints to: Office of Investor Assistance and Education, Securities and Exchange Board of India, SEBI Bhavan, Plot No. C4-A, 'G' Block, Bandra-Kurla Complex, Bandra (E), Mumbai - 400 051.

sections.heading: E. Rights of Investors
list: Right to Privacy and Confidentiality
Right to Transparent Practices
Right to fair and Equitable Treatment
Right to Adequate Information
Right to Initial and Continuing Disclosure — Right to receive information about all the statutory and regulatory disclosures.
Right to Fair & True Advertisement
Right to Awareness about Service Parameters and Turnaround Times
Right to be informed of the timelines for each service
Right to be Heard and Satisfactory Grievance Redressal
Right to have timely redressal
Right to Suitability of the Financial Products
Right to Exit from Financial product or service in accordance with the terms of agreement with the investment adviser
Right to receive clear guidance and caution notice when dealing in Complex and High-Risk Financial Products and Services
Additional Rights to vulnerable consumers — Right to get access to services in a suitable manner even if differently abled
Right to provide feedback on the financial products and services used
Right against coercive, unfair, and one-sided clauses in financial agreements

sections.heading: F. Expectations from the Investors (Responsibilities of Investors) — Do's
list: Always deal with SEBI registered Investment Advisers.
Ensure that the Investment Adviser has a valid registration certificate.
Check for SEBI registration number. Please refer to the list of all SEBI registered Investment Advisers, available on the SEBI website.

Pay only advisory fees to your Investment Adviser. Make payments of advisory fees through banking channels only and maintain duly signed receipts mentioning the details of your payments. You may make payment of advisory fees through Centralised Fee Collection Mechanism (CeFCoM) of IAASB if investment adviser has opted for the mechanism.

Always ask for your risk profiling before accepting investment advice. Insist that Investment Adviser provides advisory strictly on the basis of your risk profiling and take into account available investment alternatives.
Ask all relevant questions and clear your doubts with your Investment Adviser before acting on advice.
Assess the risk-return profile of the investment as well as the liquidity and safety aspects before making investments.

Insist on getting the terms and conditions in writing duly signed and stamped. Read these terms and conditions carefully particularly regarding advisory fees, advisory plans, category of recommendations etc. before dealing with any Investment Adviser.
Be vigilant in your transactions.
Approach the appropriate authorities for redressal of your doubts / grievances.
Inform SEBI about Investment Advisers offering assured or guaranteed returns.
Always be aware that you have the right to exit the service of an Investment Adviser.
Always be aware that you have the right to seek clarifications and clear guidance on advice.
Always be aware that you have the right to provide feedback to the Investment Adviser in respect of services received.
Always be aware that you will not be bound by any clause, prescribed by the investment adviser, which is contravening any regulatory provisions.

links.text: List of all SEBI registered Investment Advisers

sections.heading: F. Expectations from the Investors (Responsibilities of Investors) — Don'ts
list: Don't fall for stock tips offered under the pretext of investment advice.
Do not provide funds for investment to the Investment Adviser.
Don't fall for the promise of indicative or exorbitant or assured returns by the Investment Advisers. Don't let greed overcome rational investment decisions.
Don't fall prey to luring advertisements or market rumors.
Avoid doing transactions only on the basis of phone calls or messages from any Investment adviser or its representatives.
Don't take decisions just because of repeated messages and calls by Investment Advisers.
Do not fall prey to limited period discount or other incentive, gifts, etc. offered by Investment advisers.
Don't rush into making investments that do not match your risk taking appetite and investment goals.
Do not share login credential and password of your trading, demat or bank accounts with the Investment Adviser.

sections.heading: Source Document
paragraphs: This charter reflects the Investor Charter for Investment Advisers prescribed by SEBI's Master Circular for Investment Advisers, addressed to all Investment Advisers and the Investment Adviser Administration and Supervisory Body (IAASB).

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicy.subtitle: How {{adviser.tradeName}} collects, uses, and protects information submitted through this website.

sections.heading: 1. Information We Collect
paragraphs: When you use the contact form on this website, we collect the information you choose to submit: full name, email address, phone number (optional), topic of enquiry, and your message. We do not collect any financial account, banking, or KYC information through this website.

sections.heading: 2. How We Use Your Information
paragraphs: Information submitted via the contact form is used solely to respond to your enquiry. It is never sold, rented, or used for unsolicited marketing.

sections.heading: 3. Where It Is Stored & Who Processes It
paragraphs: Contact form submissions are relayed via Web3Forms directly to the Principal Officer's email inbox. Submissions are not stored in the public Google Sheet used elsewhere on this site — that sheet contains only aggregate, non-identifying SEBI complaint-count data, never contact-form or client information.

sections.heading: 4. Retention
paragraphs: Submitted information is retained in the Principal Officer's email inbox for as long as reasonably necessary to respond to and resolve your enquiry, or until you request its deletion.

sections.heading: 5. Correction & Deletion Requests
paragraphs: To request correction or deletion of information you have submitted, contact the Principal & Compliance Officer, {{founder.name}}, at {{contact.email}}.

sections.heading: 6. Third-Party Service Providers
list: Web3Forms — relays contact form submissions to our email.
Google Sheets — hosts only aggregate, public SEBI complaint-count data; no personal or contact-form data is ever placed here.
Cloudflare — domain registrar, DNS, and edge/CDN security for this website.
GitHub Pages — static hosting for this website.

sections.heading: 7. Cookies
paragraphs: This website does not use advertising or analytics cookies. Cloudflare, our edge/CDN provider, may set strictly necessary security cookies (e.g. a bot-mitigation cookie such as __cf_bm) to keep the site secure and available. This section will be updated if analytics are added in the future.

sections.heading: 8. Consent
paragraphs: By submitting the contact form on this website, you consent to your information being processed as described in this Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: 9. Changes to This Policy
paragraphs: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Material changes will be reflected on this page.

sections.heading: 1. Acceptance of Terms

sections.heading: 2. Nature of Website Content

Personalized advice is provided only to clients who have signed a formal advisory agreement following risk profiling, as required under the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations.

Registration granted by SEBI, membership of BASL and certification from NISM in no way guarantee performance of the intermediary or provide any assurance of returns to investors.

sections.heading: 5. External Links

sections.heading: 6. Limitation of Liability

sections.heading: 7. Governing Law & Jurisdiction

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Common questions about {{adviser.tradeName}} and this website.

sections.heading: What does "SEBI-Registered Investment Adviser" mean?
paragraphs: {{adviser.tradeName}} is registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) as an Investment Adviser, Reg. No. {{adviser.sebiRegNo}}. Registration means we meet SEBI's eligibility and conduct requirements for giving investment advice — it does not guarantee investment performance or returns.

sections.heading: Do you guarantee investment returns?
paragraphs: No. Investment in securities market are subject to market risks. Registration granted by SEBI, membership of BASL, and certification from NISM in no way guarantee performance or provide any assurance of returns to investors. Read all related documents carefully before investing.

sections.heading: How are your fees structured?
paragraphs: Our fee structure is published on this website once finalized. In the meantime, contact us directly for current fee details — fees are collected exclusively through banking channels, never in cash.

sections.heading: How do I raise a grievance or complaint?
paragraphs: Contact our Principal & Compliance Officer directly, or follow the Grievance Escalation Matrix, which also lists the SEBI SCORES 2.0 and SMART ODR portals for unresolved grievances.

sections.heading: Is my personal data safe?
paragraphs: See our Privacy Policy for what we collect, how it's used, and how to request correction or deletion.

sections.heading: Where can I see monthly complaint data?
paragraphs: Our Complaints Data page publishes the current month's snapshot along with monthly/annual trend and compliance audit history, as required under SEBI's Master Circular for Investment Advisers.

sections.heading: How do I get started?
paragraphs: Contact us to discuss your financial goals. Onboarding follows the process described in "Our Approach" on the homepage, including formal risk profiling and a signed client agreement with full fee disclosure.
